title: Keep the Frequency timer wordmark readable on small light-mode screens

source.ref: Frequency timer browser accessibility fixture audit, 2026-10-23

detail: The Be Still masthead used text-body (17px) in Frequency, with a 3.59:1 accent/canvas ratio. Browser axe marked it serious because that small bold text needed 4.5:1. Use the existing text-body-lg role (19px) at every viewport, preserving the mode accent, letters, weight and desktop size. The larger readable wordmark qualifies as large bold text and fits the 320px setup without wrapping or overflow. Actual SSR fixtures select SITE_DESIGN separately for each design, load compiled semantic CSS and installed Frequency sheets, and render the setup outside the members kit just as the provider does. Final eight Frequency cases (still/move, light/dark, 320/390x844) have zero axe WCAG A/AA violations; all sixteen cross-design cases have visible orb artwork and no viewport overflow. DAWN button palette contrast exceptions remain; this row does not change any global palette or waiver. Pre-fix theme/a11y sweep: 719 tests in sixty suites. Post-paint focused checks: 82 tests; post-wordmark focused checks: 25 tests, plus lint. Browser fixtures are not live production or cold-route stylesheet proof. React review found no new state, hooks, requests or bundle dependencies.

verify.note: Re-probed 2026-10-26 (meta scan SCAN-1110 follow-up): a source consequence replaces the one-off manual browser check, so a regression fails here. Original browser evidence: Browser-verified fixture: real design-specific CompactSetup and compiled app CSS, at 320/390x844 in both modes and light/dark. After the wordmark role change, all eight Frequency cases have zero axe WCAG2A/WCAG2AA/WCAG21AA violations, including color contrast, and no dialog scroll-width/height overflow. Visually inspected final Frequency light/dark 320px screenshots. Focused component tests and lint pass. DAWN palette exceptions and live-route coverage remain separately scoped.
